newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-JUDEN CELEBRATES CANADA DAY WITH ONE-HITTER FOR EXPOS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-JUDEN CELEBRATES CANADA DAY WITH ONE-HITTER FOR EXPOS.

text.p: Jeff Juden celebrated Canada Day on Tuesday by tossing a near no-hitter to carry the Montreal Expos to a 2-1 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays in Game 2 of baseball's first series between Canadian teams.

Juden allowed one hit over eight innings and struck out a career-high 14 in outdueling Roger Clemens as Canada commemorated its 130th birthday. The holiday crowd of 50,436 was the first sellout at SkyDome since 1995 Opening Day.
Juden (10-2) allowed no hits over the first seven innings and retired 19 consecutive batters until Shawn Green led off the eighth with a home run for Toronto's lone run.

After a pair of first-inning walks, Juden overpowered the Blue Jays. Prior to Green's homer, he allowed just three balls out of the infield and from the fourth through the seventh innings, he fanned nine of 12 batters.
"(Catcher) Chris Widger was calling a hell of a game," Juden said. "He made it really easy on me. We were just playing catch."
He was staked to an early 2-0 lead on a RBI double by David Segui in the first and a solo homer by Rondell White in the second and made it stand up.
Clemens (12-3) allowed two runs and 10 hits in 8 1/3 innings for his third loss in his last four decisions.
In Seattle, rookie Jose Cruz Jr. had two homers for five RBI and Alex Rodriguez belted a three-run homer to power the Mariners to a 15-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
Cruz belted a two-run homer in the second and added a three-run shot in the third for his first two-homer game.
Russ Davis added a two-run homer in the seventh in Seatle's 16-hit assault, but Ken Griffey failed to hit a home run for a season-high sixth straight game.
Jamie Moyer (8-2) allowed two runs and five hits for the win. San Francisco starter William VanLandingham (5-5) was reached for seven runs and four hits in 2 1/3 innings.

In Detroit, Bobby Higginson and Travis Fryman hit back-to-back homers in the first inning and Bob Hamelin added a three-run shot in the third as the Tigers built an eight-run lead and held on for an 8-6 victory over the New York Mets.

Higginson, who tied a club record with three homers and seven RBI in Detroit's 14-0 win Monday, homered off starter Bobby Jones (12-5), giving the Tigers a 2-0 lead. The home run was his fourth in four at-bats, tying the major-league record.
"I usually hit home runs in streaks and I guess this was just one of them," Higginson said.
Damion Easley and Curtis Pride also homered for Detroit.
In New York, Denny Neagle and Mark Wohlers combined on a six-hitter and Ryan Klesko belted a two-run homer in the sixth inning as the Atlanta Braves beat the Yankees 3-1.
Neagle (12-1) joined Jones of the Mets as the only 12-game winners in the National League. He allowed one run and six hits in 7 2/3 innings.
Wohlers worked a hitless ninth for his 18th save in 19 chances for the Braves, who had lost their last five meetings with the Yankees, dating back to last year's World Series.
Ramiro Mendoza (3-3) suffered the loss despite allowing just two runs and eight hits over seven innings.
In Baltimore, Scott Erickson allowed one run over 7 1/3 innings and Lenny Webster and Rafael Palmeiro homered as the Orioles beat the Philadelphia Phillies 4-1.

Erickson (11-3) allowed just seven hits, including five infield singles to hand the Phils their eighth straight loss. He improved to 6-1 with a 1.54 ERA at Camden Yards this season for the best home mark in the American League.
Randy Myers struck out the side in the ninth for his 26th save and 300th of his career, becoming just the ninth pitcher in history to achieve the milestone.
In Boston, Troy O'Leary had three hits and drove in three runs and Vaughn Eshelman allowed five hits over five innings as the Red Sox beat the Florida Marlins 9-2.
O'Leary had a two-run single in Boston's three-run first inning and added an RBI double in the seventh. Jesus Tavarez contributed a two-run double in a three-run eighth.

Eshelman (2-3) allowed two runs, walked one and struck out two. Florida starter Pat Rapp (4-6) lasted just three innings, allowing three runs and eight hits. He also walked six in his losing his third straight decision.
In Oakland, Jason Giambi and Scott Brosius hit two-run homers in the bottom of the eighth inning to lift the Athletics to an 8-6 victory over the San Diego Padres.
Dave Magadan also hit a two-run homer for Oakland in a three-run seventh.
Trailing 6-4 in the eighth, Oakland rallied against Doug Bochtler (1-4) and Rich Batchelor. Aaron Small (6-4) got the win by not allowing a hit over the final two innings.
San Diego jumped out to a 4-0 lead on run-scoring hits by Chris Jones, Carlos Hernandez and Quilvio Veras in a three-run fourth inning. Tony Gwynn had hits in his first four at-bats for the Padres.
